analysis_refs.heading: Viewing the boards
analysis_refs.text:
**All records are samples.** Project Gutenberg IDs, titles and the Gutenberg
rights wording are real. Every paper, author, journal, DOI (the `10.5555` test
prefix), arXiv ID and children's story is invented. Never copy board records
into fixtures as if they were real catalog data.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Navigation and routes
analysis_refs.text: | Papers | Articles, preprints, chapters (`kinds` = article, preprint, chapter, thesis, report). Query field also accepts DOI and arXiv IDs. |

analysis_refs.heading: 4. Boards
analysis_refs.text: | `PaperResults` | Paper results with type pill, title, authors, container/year, and access line naming index and host. | Pill from `kind` (+ `version` for preprints: "Preprint · v3"). Source-supplied flags ("Correction listed", "Retracted") as a second pill in `--chk`/`--err`, worded as the source's claim. Access line: "Free · Found via [index], read at [host]" when they differ; "Free · HTML, PDF at arXiv" when the index is the host. Authors truncate to three plus "+ N". |

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Discovery engines to use before broad web searching
analysis_refs.text:
Also investigate DOAJ, CORE/OpenAIRE/BASE, national libraries, professional
associations and ministry directories as leads. Choose an aggregator only after
checking current external-use terms, quotas, origin attribution and completeness.
Existing direct arXiv/DOAJ deferral remains in force until its stated constraint
has a supported solution; this plan does not quietly re-enable those connectors.

analysis_refs.text:
No paid service/store was provisioned. Account resources, credentials, activation

analysis_refs.heading: Current free live profile — 2026-11-03
analysis_refs.text:
One source is queried at a time. Signed native cursors support Show more across
process restarts without server state. Replaying makes another live request;
live indexes can change. Source throttles/timeouts remain explicit. Direct
arXiv/DOAJ automation is deferred; use their source website search links.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
All controlled machines that dispatch arXiv requests, including previews and
production, must use the **same shared coordinator and namespace**. Separate
stores would defeat its aggregate pacing rule. Never use an in-memory store
for hosted live requests. Store failures disable live dispatch; local catalogs
remain independent. Provider 429 cooldowns are shared. Cached pages and records
can still be read while a new request would be queued/limited.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not
chosen are explicit and can be searched independently from the source sheet.
DOIs select DOI-capable indexes; PMCIDs select Europe PMC using its PMCID field,
preserving the article's native MED identity. Bare versioned legacy arXiv IDs
also route directly to arXiv.
Language context is only supported by the broad adapter today; other paper
sources report unsupported rather than silently ignoring it.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
Search metadata is cached by exact source record as well as page. Opening an
arXiv result therefore uses the shared record cache instead of immediately making
another paced request. Licences remain attached to locations; a related journal
DOI is an access-unknown reference, never a substitute free copy.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
DOAJ, arXiv and OpenAlex now have bounded adapters, source-native identities and
per-location access/licence handling. Fresh [policy observations](evidence/2026-11-01/source-policies.json)
verify DOAJ's 2 RPS and arXiv's 3-second/single-connection aggregate rules. The
configured OpenAlex key reported $1/day free allowance, $0.001 ordinary search
and zero prepaid funds; runtime rechecks those conditions before dispatch.
Operational limits and caveats are in [OPERATIONS.md](OPERATIONS.md).

analysis_refs.heading: Multi-source papers follow-up
analysis_refs.text:
The [actual paper flow](evidence/2026-11-01/papers-live-flow.json) exercised a
local API, actual Redis and official source metadata: 20 + 20 unique results,
source progress, reader → save → reload → reopen, and versioned legacy arXiv
lookup → reader. The latest first response took 2,468 ms across three sources;
the next buffered page took 198 ms. This does
not establish hosted performance or provider SLAs. No browser page errors
were recorded. The test facade initially hit an OS argument-size limit; using
stdin and adding the 180 KB check fixed the facade. The production REST protocol
does not pass cache values through a command-line argument.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
All four paper adapters passed fresh [exact-record lookups](evidence/2026-11-01/exact-lookups.json)
without the record cache. Their observed times were 252–1,635 ms in this workspace;
these small samples are not SLAs. A fresh full paper flow also passed after final
changes: source progress, 20 + 20 unique records, save/reload/reopen and legacy
arXiv version lookup. The [flow report](evidence/2026-11-01/papers-live-flow.json)
records actual statuses and timing.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 3. Canonical model
analysis_refs.text:
1. Normalize exact DOI, ISBN-10/13 equivalence, PMID/PMCID and provider IDs. Valid DOI syntax does not establish existence.
2. Reconcile descriptions of the same identified version, retaining all locations and provenance. Conflicting authoritative metadata goes to review.
3. Keep translations, editions, chapters, abridgements and recordings separate. ISBN is edition-level; ISSN container-level. Missing ISBN is valid.
4. Preserve arXiv versions and Zenodo version DOI separately from concept/unversioned identifiers. Preprint and journal article can be related without being identical. Relations require source evidence.
5. Use title/author similarity only for candidate review or visual grouping, never authoritative merging.
6. Assign durable app IDs to persisted records; alias older source-native keys rather than breaking links after reconciliation.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
Phase B — initial coverage
analysis_refs.text: Add Open Textbook Library, DOAJ and arXiv; OpenAlex after key/budget verification. Then DOAB/OAPEN imports and optional Unpaywall resolver with real contact email. Keep Google/Open Library enrichment bounded.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase C — children, regional and specialist coverage
analysis_refs.text:
- Provider contracts: valid/empty/malformed response, missing fields, absent license, preview/borrow/embargo, stale links, 429/503 and schema drift.
- Identity: same DOI across indexes, preprint vs publication, arXiv versions, translations, chapter vs book, missing ISBN, unrelated same title, Zenodo concept vs version DOI.
- Search: partial/all-source failure, exhausted budget, unsupported filters, cancellation, no skipped/duplicate pages, expired cursor, honest totals.
- Imports: interrupted/repeated OAI page, tombstone, expired token, corrupt/empty bulk file and rollback.
- End-to-end: title/author/DOI, free filters, details, external HTML/reader/PDF/EPUB where offered, browser back, unchanged ISBN/library/shelf flows; launch-country checks beyond server-region behavior.
- Capacity: uncached searches/day and peak concurrency. At the observed OpenAlex price, ordinary search cost is uncached calls × $0.001; paging/enrichment add requests. arXiv 1/3 sec is at most 20/min before contention. Configure degradation before enabling traffic.

analysis_refs.heading: C07 — Preprints and working papers
analysis_refs.text:
**Retrieval strategy.** Prefer existing attributed aggregator search where its
coverage passes. The [bioRxiv/medRxiv API documentation](https://api.biorxiv.org/)
supports date-window/DOI metadata retrieval and version information; it is not a
generic keyword search interface. A permitted bounded metadata import can make
that feed searchable locally. [RePEc's metadata policy](https://ideas.repec.org/getdata.html)
prefers publisher archives/ReDIF over website scraping and requires prior contact
for commercial use. Review applicability before use; no outreach is sent as part
of this plan. Direct arXiv automation remains deferred under the current plan.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.

analysis_refs.heading: Behavior
analysis_refs.text:
Wikipedia, Wikibooks and Wikisource remain disconnected: the current robots
policies disallow the reviewed `/w/api.php` search route. No alternate route was
used to evade this restriction. arXiv/DOAJ retain their existing pacing-related
exclusion from live requests. Other registry candidates require supported query,
access or credential work before integration. This release does not make an
unverified directory or research lead searchable by merely listing it.
